content_metadata.description: A conversational interview with Tom Drivas, CEO and Director of Appia Rare Earths & Uranium Corp, conducted by Tracy Weslosky. The discussion revolves around Appia's recent resource announcement for their Brazil project, updates on their other uranium and rare earth projects, and insights into the company's future plans.

qAndA.answer: Tom Drivas is very excited to share Appia's recent achievements, particularly the impressive resource numbers from their Brazil project.
qAndA.question: What is the mood of Tom Drivas?

qAndA.answer: The project boasts very high concentrations of critical rare earth elements, specifically Neodymium and Praseodymium, surpassing many other known resources in the industry.
qAndA.question: What makes Appia's Brazil project stand out compared to other rare earth projects?

qAndA.answer: By releasing the news after the market closed on Friday, Appia aimed to provide investors ample time to process the information and conduct their research before the market reopened on Monday.
qAndA.question: Why did Appia choose to release their resource announcement on a Friday evening?

qAndA.answer: Appia is engaged in uranium exploration in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, possesses a large uranium resource in Ontario's Elliot Lake, and is involved in a rare earth project in Northern Saskatchewan.
qAndA.question: Apart from the Brazil project, what other projects is Appia currently focused on?

qAndA.answer: According to Christopher Ecclestone, an expert featured earlier in the program, the uranium market is showing signs of heating up, suggesting potential opportunities for investors.
qAndA.question: Why is there growing interest in uranium?

characterInteraction.description: Tracy and Tom engage in a conversational interview, Tracy asks questions about Appia's recent resource announcement and other projects, while Tom provides detailed answers and insights

narrativeProgression.description: The scene begins with Tracy asking Tom how he is
Tracy inquires if the drilling results are for their Ionic Clay project in Brazil and if Tom is as excited as she is
Tom shares that they have exciting news, including resource numbers, not just drilling results
Tracy asks Tom how long they have been working on this resource
Tom reveals they started drilling in July of the previous year, and within 8 months, they drilled 300 drill holes and calculated the resource with SGS
Tracy emphasizes the significance of Constantine Karayanopoulos joining Appia's advisory board, suggesting positive developments
Tracy mentions that Jack Lifton will be interviewed tomorrow and steers the conversation back to the high numbers of Neodymium and Praseodymium
Tracy highlights the timing of the press release, issued on Friday evening after the market close, giving people a couple of days to analyze the results
Tracy asks what shareholders should expect next after the Brazil project's resource announcement
Tom outlines their plans: focusing on metallurgy, further drilling, and eventually preparing a preliminary economic assessment of the deposit
Tracy prompts an update on Appia's Saskatchewan rare earth and uranium projects
Tom discusses their four uranium exploration properties around the Athabasca Basin in Saskatchewan and plans for further exploration
Tom mentions their large uranium resource in Ontario's Elliot Lake, with 55 million tonnes of uranium in inferred and indicated categories
Tracy reminds viewers of the importance of uranium, as Christopher Ecclestone had earlier suggested the market is heating up, and reminds them that Appia is also involved in the rare earth industry
Tracy concludes the interview, encouraging viewers to visit Appia's website for more information, and congratulates Tom on the resource announcement

We have got very high numbers. As I said, in terms of the high grade portion of 13 and a half million tones. We have got 1,300 ppm magnet rare earths, basically, which is more than some other resources, basically, some other companies that have a total rare earth oxides.

And at some point we're going to look at the P.A. basically. So better look at once we got a better handle of the malergy, the recoveries, then we'll, you know, the next step would be to a preliminary assessment of the deposit.

youtube_description:
In this interview with Tracy Weslosky during PDAC 2024, Tom Drivas, CEO and Director of Appia Rare Earths & Uranium Corp. (CSE: API | OTCQX: APAAF) discussed the results from the maiden Mineral Resource Estimate for Appia’s PCH Ionic Adsorption Clay Project in Brazil. Announcing a significant 52.8 million tonnes of resource, Tom highlighted the presence of extremely high-grades of rare earths within this resource, showcasing some of the highest TREO (total rare earth oxide) grades globally.

Tom emphasized the project's potential, stating, "We have only explored 1% of the total area... We have 40,000 hectares." Tom also highlighted the project's richness in magnet rare earths like neodymium and praseodymium, essential for producing permanent magnets in high demand. The addition of industry experts like Constantine Karayannopoulos, Jack Lifton and Don Hains, P. Geo to Appia’s Advisory Board underscores the project's significance and potential.

Besides the project in Brazil, Appia is also advancing uranium exploration properties around the Athabasca Basin in Saskatchewan and has a significant uranium resource in Ontario at Elliot Lake. Notably, the company is also advancing its Alces Lake project in Saskatchewan, renowned for its high-grade critical rare earths in monazite.

About Appia Rare Earths & Uranium Corp.

Appia is a publicly traded Canadian company in the rare earth element and uranium sectors. The Company is currently focusing on delineating high-grade critical rare earth elements and gallium on the Alces Lake property, as well as exploring for high-grade uranium in the prolific Athabasca Basin on its Otherside, Loranger, North Wollaston, and Eastside properties. The Company holds the surface rights to exploration for 94,982.39 hectares (234,706.59 acres) in Saskatchewan. The Company also has a 100% interest in 13,008 hectares (32,143 acres), with rare earth elements and uranium deposits over five mineralized zones in the Elliot Lake Camp, Ontario. Lastly, the Company holds the right to acquire up to a 70% interest in the PCH Project (See June 9th, 2023 Press Release – Click HERE) which is 40,963.18 ha. in size and located within the Goiás State of Brazil. (See January 11th, 2024 Press Release – Click HERE)
